I have farmed this land for 30 years, and I know every corner of my 4.1 mu. I only finished middle school, but I learned more from the field than from any book. Last year my cotton gave me about 250 kg per mu, and the stevia dried leaves sold for decent money at the county market. This year I will stick close to that, because with seven people in the house and only 4 mu, I cannot afford a bad guess.

My neighbor across the road planted an improved cotton seed last spring, and his bolls were noticeably bigger at harvest. I saw it myself, so this year I bought the same variety from the village input store. It costs more than the old seed, but I trust my own eyes. For stevia, I use my own traditional cuttings like always. I know this plant; changing it would be foolish.

For cotton on 2 mu: I will do rotary tillage first and break up the soil properly. For fertilizer, I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base — that is 50 kg. Then I top-dress twice with urea, about 12 kg each time. Adding it up, that is about 18 kg nitrogen per mu, 7 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium. I irrigate 4 times from my well: after sowing, at flowering, at boll-setting, and once more in August if it stays dry. Cotton always has worms and aphids, so I spray 6 times. I rent the spray machine from the cooperative, 5 yuan per mu each pass.

For stevia on 2.1 mu: Rotary tillage too. This leaf crop is lighter feeding. I give it 30 kg compound fertilizer per mu as base, then one top-dress of 15 kg urea. That comes to about 11 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. Stevia leaves need water to stay tender, so I irrigate 5 times through the season. Pests are fewer than on cotton, so 3 sprays is enough. Last year I got about 200 kg dried leaves per mu, and I expect the same this year.

The input dealer tried to sell me extra fertilizer last week, saying I would get 50 kg more yield. But urea is 125 yuan per bag now, and my son works in a factory in Handan — he sends money home, but I am not wasting it. I watched what three other families around me do, and they all use roughly these amounts. If I use too little I might lose yield, but if I use too much I throw away cash. With a small farm, every yuan matters. I would rather copy my neighbors and sleep easy.
